title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: params, streaming stability, function-calls and structured output
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers expect parity with the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions API for both compatibility and migration. This PR implements a compatibility layer and runtime mappings for chat parameters (roles/user field, stop sequences, logprobs, echo, n, temperature/top_p, penalties), improves streaming stability for long-lived SSE/HTTP2 connections, and adds initial function-calling semantics + structured output hints. The approach is additive: default behavior remains Redwood's modern chat API, but when an OpenAI-compatible request is detected (path /v1/chat.completions or compat flag), we translate parameters to the internal request model and apply compatibility-preserving semantics.

What this PR does (summary): 1) Parameter parity: map OpenAI params to internal fields (temperature, top_p, n, stop, logprobs, echo, max_tokens, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, user). Implemented nuanced behavior for stop sequences (multi-token aware, applies after model emits full token) and logprobs (best-effort mapping for supported models). 2) Role/user mapping: accept messages with "role":"system|user|assistant|tool" and set internal channel/metadata accordingly; preserve user field in telemetry. 3) Function calling: add experimental support for OpenAI-style function_call object to request routing and structured output hints; runtime returns a synthetic "function_call" token stream when applicable and stores function_call metadata in response JSON. 4) Streaming stability: improved chunk buffering, keepalive ping frames, and more tolerant reconnect handling to avoid duplicate finalization events when clients reconnect mid-stream. Also added a configurable compatibility mode that yields the exact SSE fields expected by common OpenAI clients (id, choices[*].delta, finish_reason). 5) SDK and doc changes: Python/TS SDK compatibility stubs and README sections describing differences and migration steps. 6) Tests: unit tests covering stop/echo/logprobs, e2e streaming tests with simulated disconnects, and integration tests for function_call roundtrip. 7) Observability: add new metrics for compat-mode requests and a small dashboard update to redwood-console defaults.

Notes on compatibility tradeoffs: - For models without native logprobs we return null and emit a compatibility warning in response.meta. - stop sequences are enforced at token-boundary where possible; we added two new tests to validate behavior across tokenizers used in our curated model set. - function_call is opt-in; we surface the raw function_call payload (name/arguments) in the response metadata when running in compat mode.

References: Linear ENG-5281 (chat parity), ENG-5310 (streaming robustness), SUP-987 (customer incident investigating tool-calling mismatch).

files_changed: server/http/handlers/openai_compat.go - added request translation, validation, logging
diff_snippets: runtime/streaming/stream_manager.go: changed flushThreshold from 256 -> 128 and added keepaliveTicker
runtime/model/stop_handler.go: Inserted tokenizer-aware stop check: if matchEndsOnTokenBoundary(tokenStream, stop) -> truncate
review_comments: Arjun Patel (review): The stop-sequence behavior needs precise semantics for multi-token stops. Can we add tests covering spaces/byte-level splits?

Maya Chen (reply): Added three new tokenizer fixtures and unit tests in tests/unit/stop_handler_test.go covering leading/trailing space and BPE splits. Also added an integration test against our GPT-like tokenizer. See commit c3d4e5f.

Priya Nair (review): function_call integration looks promising but I want clearer docs on the security implications when executing returned function arguments. Please add guidance for validating function inputs.

Maya Chen (reply): Expanded docs/openai_compat.md with a "Function execution safety" section describing recommended validation, timeouts, and sandboxing. Also included a code sample for a safe dispatch wrapper.
Diego Morales (review): Did the streaming fixes increase CPU usage under high concurrency? Please add microbenchmarks.

Maya Chen (reply): Added a microbenchmark in perf/bench_streaming.go; results show ~3% CPU increase at p95 under very aggressive keepalive config, but end-to-end tail latency improved due to fewer duplicate reconnect reconciliations. Benchmarks and raw data attached to ENG-5310.
Liam O'Connor (approval): Approving after tests and docs updated. Nice work on handling edge cases for stop/logprobs.
ci_log_summary: CI initially failed: tests/e2e/chat_compat_streaming_test.go flaky on race. Root cause was a missing lock in stream_manager; fixed and rerun. Lint flagged an unused import in sdk/python; fixed. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, e2e, linters, integration).
merge_outcome: Merged by squash on 2026-03-01. Commit message consolidated key changes and references ENG-5281/ENG-5310. No revert required post-merge.
release_notes: Added OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility mode: parameter parity (temperature, top_p, n, stop, logprobs, echo, user), experimental function_call passthrough, improved streaming stability for long-lived connections, and SDK compatibility shims. See docs/openai_compat.md for migration steps and differences. (ENG-5281)
post_merge_actions: Open: add compat-mode API key telemetry filter for PII review (security)
Follow-up: extend logprobs support to quantized models (ENG-5402)
Follow-up: add TS SDK streaming example that mirrors openai-streaming-client behavior
qa_notes: E2E verified with a small set of OpenAI-compatible clients (python requests, node fetch polyfill). Verified stop/echo/logprobs behavior against reference harness. Streaming reconnection tested by injecting network faults; observed single finalization event for 99/100 runs after fix.
security_considerations: Function_call is opt-in; docs include guidance on sanitizing arguments before executing. We log function_call metadata but not function arguments by default (configurable). Added a gating flag in the control plane for enterprise installs.
notes_for_backports: Backport to release/2026-02 required for customers on Dedicated who requested OpenAI parity. Exclude perf microbenchmark changes when backporting to v1.2 branch.
author_notes: This is intentionally conservative: compat mode aims to be predictable for migration, not to replace our native API. Please flag any client behaviors we missed; we can iterate on corner cases.
